summary: Makes the Options page extendable so downstream projects can add their own cards and store global project config through hardened, Dlux-first extension points. Apps register Options cards through a secure code-only registry (register_card, autodiscovered from each app's optional dlux_options.py at startup) — so a card can never be injected via a request, a stored value, or a non-superuser — with server-side permission/superuser gating, sandboxed rendering (a broken card is skipped, never blanks the page), and a dlux:options-ready lifecycle event for attaching card JS; the built-in cards are untouched. Adds a superuser-only, namespace-scoped app-owned system-config endpoint writing only SystemSettings.extra_config['app'][namespace] (size-capped, audit-logged, cache-cleared) plus a get_app_system_config() read helper. Inline-safe: no migration, JSON/view/static/template updates only.
highlights: Extendable Options page: downstream apps add cards via a secure registry (register_card + autodiscovered dlux_options.py) — registration is code-only so cards can't be injected via HTTP/data — with server-side permission gating, sandboxed rendering, and a dlux:options-ready lifecycle event; built-in cards untouched.
App-owned system config: superuser-only, namespace-scoped endpoint writing SystemSettings.extra_config['app'][ns] (size-capped, audited, cache-cleared) plus a get_app_system_config() read helper.
Adding a card is minimal: create <yourapp>/dlux_options.py, call register_card(id, title, template_name, ...), and your template renders as the card body inside the standard card chrome.

Cards support config-driven visibility (a fail-closed visible() predicate) and declarative persistence: a control marked data-dlux-app-pref auto-saves to the user's app-pref namespace and fires dlux:app-pref-changed for live updates.

Translation hygiene: table columns can now use model-qualified headers (tbl_{model}_{column}) for distinct labels, and 88 duplicate keys were unified into a backward-compatible alias map (get_strings resolves retired keys to their canonical), with dev scripts to find unused/duplicate strings and apply the unification.
